summary.tldr: Adds a second option for the citizenship oath, letting people swear loyalty to Canada instead of only to the King.
what_it_does: Replaces the current oath rule with a new section that lets a person use either of two oath wordings.
Keeps one version of the oath that swears allegiance to King Charles III and says the person will follow Canada’s laws and Constitution.
Adds a second version that swears allegiance to Canada instead of to the King, while keeping the same promise to follow Canada’s laws and Constitution.
Repeals the existing schedule that set out one oath wording.
Brings the change into force the day after royal assent.
summary.background: Under the current Citizenship Act, the oath is set out in a schedule. This bill repeals that schedule and replaces it with two oath options.
